title: Fastest Guided Route (A* Pathfinding)
real_world_story: A delivery drone must cross a large city grid with no-fly zones. Plain BFS checks too many blocks, so the flight controller uses straight-line distance as a guess to steer the search toward the landing pad.

real_world_connection.input_represents: City grid where 0 is flyable airspace and 1 is a no-fly zone
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: A* search guided by Manhattan distance toward the landing pad

problem_statement: Given an R x C maze grid of 0 (free) and 1 (wall), a start cell (sr, sc) and a destination cell (dr, dc), find the minimum number of steps from start to destination using 4-directional moves. Implement A* search with the Manhattan-distance heuristic h(r, c) = |r - dr| + |c - dc|.
task: Return the minimum number of steps from start to destination, or -1 if unreachable.
input_format: The first line contains two integers R and C. The next R lines each contain C integers (0 or 1). The final line contains four integers sr sc dr dc.
output_format: Print the minimum number of steps, or -1 if unreachable.

examples.explanation: A* with Manhattan distance finds the same 4-step shortest route: right, right, down, down.

expected_algorithm.name: A* Pathfinding
expected_algorithm.reason: Manhattan distance never overestimates on a 4-directional grid, so A* stays optimal while expanding fewer cells than BFS by aiming at the goal.

hint: Priority of a cell is f = g + h where g is steps so far and h is Manhattan distance.
Pop the smallest-f cell from a min-heap.
Skip walls, out-of-bounds cells, and cells already reached with a smaller g.
real_world_takeaway: A* gives optimal grid routes like BFS but reaches the goal faster by following a distance heuristic.
